haiku-low.q1: It returns 202 only after the Raw log confirms the replicated append. The body lists rejected event_ids. Malformed events go to a reject bucket with a reason.
haiku-low.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on, up to 5 min.
haiku-low.q3: The first copy received is kept. Later copies are dropped, even if they arrive up to 7 days later.
haiku-low.q4: Tuesday. A day is the UTC date of received_at, which the Collector stamps. The client timestamp never decides the day, so it belongs to Tuesday's partition and replay.
haiku-low.q5: In the Dedup store, the key-value store's dedup namespace. Each event_id maps to its Raw-log position. An 8-day TTL removes old entries.
haiku-low.q6: The processor pauses and retries the micro-batch with backoff, never letting events through unchecked. Events wait in the Raw log, and the Collector keeps accepting them.
haiku-low.q7: On rereading, the same positions are found and kept. The merge on event_id overwrites rows instead of adding them, so nothing is lost or doubled.
haiku-low.q8: Only the archive files under archive/date=D/, plus read-only event_id lookups in events_clean. Rebuilt rows go to table events_clean_staging_D, then swap into partition D.
haiku-low.q9: It keeps the earliest received_at copy per event_id within D, then drops any event_id already in events_clean for D-7 to D-1. It never uses the Dedup store.
haiku-low.q10: events_clean is untouched and still serves the old D. Recovery: drop the staging table, release replay:D, and rerun. If the swap itself fails, the old partition stays and the swap is retried.
haiku-low.q11: Only closed days: at least 02:00 UTC on D+1, with archive/date=D/_COMPLETE present, and D within the 90-day archive. Also the live processor must be past D's last event.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for the decision. Product has not decided whether suspected bots are dropped or kept with a flag. Bot events stay in the archive either way.

sonnet.q1: It acknowledges with 202 only after the Raw log confirms the replicated append; valid events are appended, malformed ones go to the reject bucket, and the 202 body lists the rejected event_ids.
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... up to 5 min. Mobile events still unacknowledged after 7 days are discarded; rejected events are never retried.
sonnet.q3: The first copy received is kept; later copies are dropped, even if they arrive up to 7 days later.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday (UTC date of received_at, 00:10 Tuesday); the client timestamp doesn't decide the day. It belongs to Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay.
sonnet.q5: In the Dedup store (the key-value store's dedup namespace). Key is event_id, value is the first copy's Raw-log position (partition + offset). The 8-day TTL removes old entries.
sonnet.q6: The live processor pauses and retries with backoff and never lets events through unchecked. Events wait in the Raw log (14-day retention), the Collector keeps accepting and acknowledging them, and an alert fires at 5 min of lag.
sonnet.q7: The position isn't committed, so it rereads the micro-batch. Dedup finds the key holding the same position and keeps the event (not dropped as a duplicate), and the merge on event_id overwrites existing rows instead of adding new ones. Nothing is lost or doubled.
sonnet.q8: Input is only the archive files under archive/date=D/ (plus read-only event_id lookups in events_clean for D-7..D-1). Rebuilt events are written to the staging table events_clean_staging_D before the swap.
sonnet.q9: Within D, keep for each event_id the copy with the earliest received_at (tie: lowest Raw-log position). Then drop any event_id already in events_clean for days D-7 ... D-1, since its first copy arrived on an earlier day.
sonnet.q10: events_clean is untouched and still serves the old D. Recovery: drop the staging table, release the replay:D lock, and rerun from the start. (If only the swap fails, the old partition stays and the swap is retried.)
sonnet.q11: A day D that is closed (at least 02:00 UTC on D+1) with archive/date=D/_COMPLETE present, that the live processor has committed past, within the 90-day archive, and with no other replay of D running.
sonnet.q12: Undecided: Product hasn't decided whether suspected bots are dropped or kept with a flag (open question, would go in step 5). Bot events stay in the archive either way.
